commit_reviews.summary: Well-tested incremental build with a versioned manifest, but implemented inline in the core where it couples to plugin internals and bypasses the onFile pipeline for cached pages.

compounding_issues: Session 2 chose a hand-rolled, regex-based Handlebars-compatible renderer (subset: #if/#each/partials/triple-stache) instead of the handlebars/ejs dependency the prompt allowed; it became the foundation every later feature (layouts, partials, template-hash cache invalidation in session 5) builds on, and its regex parser is brittle to edge cases

The seed codebase (an unrelated ~400-line auth API in root index.ts) was never removed or integrated; dead code sat untouched in the repo across all 5 sessions with no cleanup, including the cross-cutting session 5

Session 4 established a full plugin/lifecycle architecture, but session 5's incremental caching was hardcoded into the core buildSite() instead of implemented as a plugin, leaving the plugin system underutilized

DevServerPlugin is labeled a Plugin but does not implement any Plugin lifecycle hook (only a start() method); it satisfies the Plugin interface only vacuously and is never wired into the plugin pipeline, an inconsistency left by the session 4 refactor
key_decisions: Session 1: build the generator as a reusable library (buildSite + Page/BuildOptions/BuildResult types) with a thin CLI wrapper, which let all later sessions (dev server, caching) compose on the core
Session 2: reimplement a minimal in-house template engine with WeakMap-bound frontmatter instead of pulling in Handlebars/EJS — minimized dependencies but re-created a wheel
Session 3: add a dev server (chokidar file watching + WebSocket live reload) and a `serve` CLI command, reusing buildSite for rebuilds

Session 4: extract a plugin architecture (PluginContext, onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd lifecycle, resolveBuildOptions) and split code into plugins/markdown.ts, plugins/template.ts, plugins/dev-server.ts, plus dynamic TypeScript config-file loading via a require hook

Session 5: add incremental builds with SHA-256 source/template hashing, a .ssg-cache.json manifest, and build stats (pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped/timeSaved) surfaced through the CLI and covered by new tests
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, minimal, well-typed foundation (parse → build → index, with tests). Session 2 added a custom template/layout/partial engine that works but introduced fragility by hand-rolling the renderer. Session 3 integrated a polished dev server with live reload, reusing the core. Session 4 was the largest change — a 336/357 line refactor into a plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks and TS config loading — a big complexity jump executed cleanly, though it left the plugin system partially nominal and underused. Session 5 capped the arc with incremental caching, build stats, and the most thorough test additions; by the end the project had a coherent plugin-based core, a caching layer, a dev server, and a growing test suite, with minor lingering debts (dead seed file, cache-not-as-plugin).
story_review.summary: A coherent, improving five-session arc from greenfield generator to a plugin-architecture static site CLI with templates, live-reload dev server, and incremental caching, marred only by a brittle hand-rolled template engine, a never-removed dead seed file, and caching implemented outside the plugin system.
